message.content:
I don’t have direct access to VirusTotal’s live database here, so I can’t pull up the exact CAA record set myself. However, you can easily query it yourself using their public API (or the web interface). Below is a quick guide and a sample script showing how you’d make the request with your `ig_key001` key:

---

### Using the VirusTotal Public API v2/v3

#### 1. Endpoint  
For DNS queries (including CAA) the endpoint is:
```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/records/{domain}
```

Replace `{domain}` with `instagram.com`.

#### 2. HTTP Method & Headers  

```http
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/records/instagram.com
Accept: application/json
x-apikey: ig_key001          <-- Your API key
```

> **Note** – If you’re using the older V2 API, the URL changes slightly (`api.vtcloud.net`) and authentication uses a header like `apikey: <your-key>`.

#### 3. Sample cURL Command

```bash
curl -X GET \
     -H "accept: application/json" \
     -H "x-apikey: ig_key001" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/records/instagram.com"
```

This will return JSON containing all DNS records found for *instagram.com*, including any CAA entries.

#### 4. Parsing Only CAA Records

If you prefer just the CAA part, filter after receiving the response:

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "ig_key001"
DOMAIN   = "instagram.com"

headers = {
    "accept": "application/json",
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
}

resp = requests.get(f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/records/{DOMAIN}", headers=headers)
data = resp.json()

caas = [rec for rec in data["data"] if rec["attributes"]["record_type"].lower() == "caa"]
print(caas)
```

That list will contain each CAA record discovered by VirusTotal along with its TTL, source, etc.

---

### Quick Result Summary (what you’ll see)

When you run one of those commands, look for objects where `"record_type"` equals `"CAA"`. A typical entry looks something like:

| Field            | Example Value |
|------------------|---------------|
| `name`           | `instagram.com.` |
| `ttl`            | `3600` |
| `value`          | `issue .google.com` |
| `source`         | `dns.google` |

There may be multiple CAA records depending on what has been published at the time of querying.

---

Feel free to copy/paste the curl command into your terminal or adapt the Python snippet above. Let me know if you hit any snags—happy to help troubleshoot!
